q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures.
e: True. All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures. A pure substance has a fixed composition, either an element or a compound.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a variable composition.
e: False. It is not true that a pure substance is a form of matter that always has a variable composition. A pure substance has a fixed composition, not a variable one.

q: John Dalton proposed the theory of matter at the beginning of the 19th century.
e: True. John Dalton proposed the theory of matter at the beginning of the 19th century. Dalton treated atoms as the tiny particles that make up elements.

q: According to John Dalton, atoms were visible and divisible.

q: Modern experimental evidence has shown that atoms are indivisible.
e: False. It is not true that modern experimental evidence has shown that atoms are indivisible. Modern experimental evidence has shown that atoms are divisible.

q: The atom is still considered as the basic unit of any element.
e: True. The atom is still considered as the basic unit of any element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: A molecule is the smallest unit of any substances that possesses the properties of that substance.
